messages.text: I filled out the RSA. I have received no response

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Your form went through, so the request is on file, and I'm picking up the technical side now.

A blown fuse plus "LCD lights on USB-C but the fans only twitch" splits two ways: a power supply that can't hold the current, or a fault on the board itself. One check tells us which:

1. Plug the NerdQaxe++ into a different USB-C power supply rated at least 5V/4A (a decent laptop or tablet charger with a quality cable, not a phone brick).
2. Watch it for about 30 seconds from the moment it powers up.

Then tell me which one happens:
- fans spin up properly and the UI shows chips/hashrate
- same twitching, screen on, no hashing
- nothing at all

If you can, a short video of that power-up plus a clear photo of the serial sticker on the back would let me settle it in one go rather than asking again.
Handed to the team · Customer filled the RMA form weeks ago with no reply; needs JD's eyes on the fau

You're right, and weeks of silence on a form is not okay. I'm sorry.

I've put your case in front of JD, our hardware lead, with everything on it: NerdQaxe++ from Shop····, blown fuse replaced, LCD lights on USB-C, fans only twitch, no hashing. He picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

Two things that will make his call immediate rather than another round of questions:
1. A short video of the unit powering up (the twitching fans and the screen).
2. Whether you've already tried a different USB-C supply rated 5V/4A or better.

A blown fuse on this board usually means a short, which is not something you fix with settings. If that second supply does nothing either, that is the answer and I'll say so plainly.

Faster route if you want it tonight: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, and mention @nullhashrate, that's JD. He and the community are very active there.
I tried various power supplies.  Still just the twitching fans.  I pluged the LCD into a USB-C and it powers on.  It says there is some power fault
